scenes.text: Want your records to sound good for decades? Here is how to care for vinyl in four steps.
First, store them upright on a sturdy shelf. Records stacked flat can warp under their own weight.
Handle every record by its edges and the label, so skin oils never touch the grooves.
Before each play, give the spinning record a pass with a carbon fibre brush to lift dust.
Finally, keep them away from heat and direct sunlight, which can warp the vinyl.

steps.label: Store them upright
steps.headline: Keep them *standing.*
steps.tip: Stacked flat, the records at the bottom take all the weight and can warp.

steps.label: Hold by the edges
steps.headline: Edges and label *only.*
steps.tip: Skin oils left in the grooves attract dust and add surface noise.

steps.label: Brush before playing
steps.headline: Dust off every *spin.*
steps.tip: A light pass while the platter turns lifts loose dust before the needle finds it.

steps.label: Keep it cool
steps.headline: No heat, no *sun.*
steps.tip: Vinyl softens with heat, so a sunny shelf can warp a record.
